requirement:
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph is text of its section. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
rationale:
**Judgment: the requirement is met.** The comment-ownership rules are implemented in `src/outline/mod.rs`, and every consumer of the owner assignment is marked `{impl}`. Tests cover each rule across languages. I found one small unlikely edge case that I do not count as a gap.

## Implementation

**Profiles**
- Each language profile defines what a comment is. `Profile` (`src/outline/profile.rs`) has `is_comment` and `comment_binds_to_container`.
- Markdown's `is_comment` (`src/outline/markdown.rs`) accepts only `html_block` nodes that start with `<!--` and end with `-->`. An inline HTML comment inside a paragraph is therefore not a comment and stays text of its section.
- Rust marks `//!` and `/*!` comments as container-bound via `is_inner_doc_comment` (`src/outline/rust.rs`). The other profiles (CSS, Markdown, Python, TOML, TypeScript, TSX, YAML) use `never`.

**Run formation (`assign_comments`, `src/outline/mod.rs`)**
- Two comments join one run only when all of these hold:
  - they have the same container-binding;
  - neither follows code on its line (`trails_code`);
  - only whitespace lies between them;
  - the second starts on the line right after the first ends.
- Comments on consecutive lines therefore form one run. A comment after other source on its line, including another comment, forms a run by itself.

**Ownership**
- A trailing comment goes to the innermost node covering its line (`trailing_owner`), or to the root when no node covers it.
- Any other run goes to the next child that starts after it within the smallest containing node, or to that container if there is none (`run_owner`). At top level the container is the root.
- A container-bound run goes to the smallest containing node, so a file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root.

**Consumers**
- Fence comments use the run's owner: `comment_fences` in `src/fenced.rs`.
- `owner_at_line` in `src/outline/mod.rs` assigns a reference to its owning node. It is used by:
  - `reference_selector` in `src/authoring/inputs.rs`, for authoring inputs;
  - `reference_set_digest` in `src/evidence.rs`;
  - `citation_items` in `src/citations.rs`.
- The line-selection helpers `comment_owners_at_line`, `nodes_for_lines` and `nodes_for_range` all use the owners.
- All of these, and the profile statics, carry `{impl}` markers.

**Edge case**
- `owner_at_line` returns the first comment owner on a line. A line holding two comments with different owners, such as `/* a */ /* {impl}… */`, could attribute a reference in the second comment to the first one's owner.
- This is contrived. Fence ownership (`comment_fences`) uses the exact run owner. I do not count it as a gap.

## Tests

All are in `src/outline/tests.rs` unless noted.
- `comment_runs_belong_to_the_next_node_or_their_container` covers these cases:
  - a comment before a node, between nodes, and inside a body;
  - a trailing comment;
  - a floating comment in a container;
  - `//!` module docs;
  - a final top-level comment.
- `comment_between_two_fns_belongs_to_the_next` and `trailing_comment_after_last_fn_in_mod_belongs_to_the_mod` cover the next-node and container fallbacks.
- `top_level_comment_with_nothing_after_belongs_to_the_root` covers the root fallback.
- `comment_after_code_on_a_line_belongs_to_that_lines_node` covers trailing comments in nested nodes.
- `file_level_inner_doc_comments_and_unmapped_code_belong_to_the_root` covers `//!` and `/*!` at file level.
- `comment_runs_follow_the_same_rules_in_every_language` covers Python, TypeScript, TSX, CSS, TOML, YAML and Markdown.
- `markdown_comments_are_html_comment_blocks_not_inline_comments` covers the Markdown inline-versus-block rule.
- `a_comment_after_another_comment_on_its_line_forms_its_own_run` covers the "including another comment" case.
- The two YAML tests (`yaml_comments_before_a_key_belong_to_that_key_not_the_previous_one` and `workflow_job_marks_belong_to_the_job_that_follows`) cover YAML's trailing-comment folding.
- Consumer tests:
  - `comment_fences_close_within_one_comment_run` in `src/fenced.rs`;
  - `references_contribute_their_owning_outline_nodes` in `src/authoring/inputs.rs`;
  - `reference_set_digest_tracks_impl_and_test_edges_by_node` in `src/evidence.rs`;
  - `search_returns_innermost_nodes_and_comment_owners` in `src/authoring/tools.rs`.

There are no acknowledged FIXMEs.

between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top

{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` and

:::{req} rust_item_coverage

During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file in the project: every `.rs` file except those under `.git` or `target` directories at any depth or under the project-root `book`, `evidence`, or `vendor` directories. Every explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and every struct, enum, and union MUST have a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example, or a valid citation of the built-in `habeas:none` under {cite}`requirements.references.no_requirement`, in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report every unreferenced item with its file, line, kind, and name, and MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file.
:::{req} authoring_inputs
When authoring evidence, the edges defined by
{cite}`requirements.references.targets` MUST determine the reference
contributions to the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`. The target of each edge leaving
the assessed subject MUST contribute; sources with only edges into the subject
MUST NOT contribute and remain discoverable under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index`. A `{cite}` made by the subject
contributes the cited definition's complete fenced declaration. An anchor under
{cite}`requirements.references.anchors` contributes the complete anchored file.
An in-source `{impl}` or `{test}` reference to the subject contributes the source
containing it: for a reference in a supported language, the smallest enclosing
outline node under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; for a reference in a Markdown requirement, example, or
terminology declaration, that complete declaration; for other references, the
complete containing source file. Literal references, evidence copies, and
generated output MUST remain excluded under the existing reference-discovery
rules.
These contribution rules MUST apply only to edges directly leaving the assessed
subject. Including another declaration or source MUST NOT by itself recursively
expand that source's own edges. Reference links MUST NOT be described as proof
that all substantively relevant sources have been found.
